# drop-buoy

Drop a buoy: capture one task as a work item in this repo's tracker — well-written and linked to related work, without duplicating what already exists — so something that surfaced mid-sail isn't lost and doesn't derail the current work.

## When the main agent uses this

*(Spawned as the capture **worker** and told to run the Procedure? Do that — skip this section.)*

When you (the main Claude) are working and notice incidental work — cleanup, something confusing, a case not covered, a follow-up idea — **don't derail.** Fork a subagent to run this skill, and keep working:

```
Agent(
  subagent_type: "general-purpose",
  description: "capture task",
  prompt: "Invoke the `drop-buoy` skill (`seamapping:drop-buoy` in this project) and run its
           Procedure directly — you are the worker subagent; do not fork again. Capture this task:
           <what you noticed>. It came up while <current work>. Report back the captured item's handle and any links."
)
```

The subagent does the search + create + link and reports the handle. You mention it to Jessitron in one line and move on. For an explicit "track this" from Jessitron, you can run the procedure directly instead of forking.

## Procedure (self-contained — assume none of the main conversation's context)

1. **Find the seamap & resolve the adapter.** Read `./SEAMAP.md`. No file, or no `## Tracking`
   section, → this repo isn't set up to capture work: say so (suggest `begin-voyage` /
   `establish-tracking`) and stop. Do **not** guess a backend. Otherwise resolve `## Tracking` per
   `../../TRACKING-ADAPTER.md` (paths here are relative to this skill's own directory): a
   `backend: <name>` shorthand resolves to `../../adapters/<name>.md`; prose lists the operations
   inline. drop-buoy uses two operations:
   `list-open` (to find related work) and `capture` (to record the new item).

2. **Load the operations' tools.** Load whatever tools the resolved adapter says `list-open` and
   `capture` use. Stock `in-repo` needs no tool loading — it's Read and Edit on `TODO.md`. Stock
   `linear`: ToolSearch the *bare* names `list_issues`, `save_issue` — don't hardcode the server
   prefix, it varies by install.

3. **Search for related work** with `list-open`, passing keywords from the new task. Read the
   results; decide which are genuinely related (same area, a dependency, or overlap). If one is a
   near-duplicate, **update it instead** (the `update` operation) of capturing a new item.

4. **Write the item well.** A captured task is only as useful as its description. Include:
   - **Title** — concise, imperative ("Validate deck IDs before load").
   - **What surfaced it** — the task / session / context it came from.
   - **Why it matters** — the cost of not doing it, or the value of doing it.
   - Enough context that future-Jessitron understands it cold, with no memory of this session.

5. **Capture it.** Call `capture` with the `title`, the `body` (the write-up from step 4), and
   `priority` if known. The adapter records it in this repo's tracker and returns the new item's
   `handle`.

6. **Link honestly** — via `capture`'s `links` (related / parent / blocks / blockedBy), each a
   `handle` from step 3.
   - **related** — for the genuinely-related items found in step 3.
   - **parent** — only if this is genuinely a sub-task of one.
   - **blocks / blockedBy** — only for a _real_ dependency.
   - **Never invent structure** to look tidy. A missing link is fine; a fake dependency is not.

7. **Report back:** the new item's `handle`, its title, and any links you created.

## Conventions & gotchas

- **Backend mechanics live in the adapter**, not here. Identifier/handle formats, append-only
  relations, the create-vs-update distinction, and any stale-response gotchas are documented in the
  resolved adapter (e.g. `../../adapters/linear.md`). This skill only names operations.
- **Prefer linking/relating over duplicating.** A duplicate is worse than a missing link.
- **One effort, one project.** Setting up the tracking project itself is `establish-tracking`'s
  job, not this one.

# Stock adapter: `linear`

Selected by `## Tracking` shorthand `- backend: linear`. An **opt-in** backend for projects that
want a hosted tracker with relations, milestones, and a web UI. The default is `in-repo`; choose
this one deliberately, knowing every operation costs an MCP round-trip.

Implements the port in `../TRACKING-ADAPTER.md`. Read that for the operation return shapes.

## Coordinates

Read from the `## Tracking` section of the repo's `SEAMAP.md`:

- `project` — the Linear project. Write it as a **markdown link** to the project so a human reading
  `SEAMAP.md` can click straight through; the adapter reads the **link text** as the project name and
  ignores the href. (A bare name with no link also works.) **Required.**
- `team` — the Linear team name (e.g. `jessitron`). **Required.**

Example:

```markdown
## Tracking
- backend: linear
- project: [Personal task system](https://linear.app/honeycombio/project/personal-task-system)
- team: jessitron
```

## Loading the tools

The Linear MCP tools are deferred — load their schemas before calling. **Don't hardcode the server
prefix**: it varies by install (`mcp__linear-server__…`, `mcp__claude_ai_Linear__…`, …). Search by
the bare operation name and use whatever matches:

```
ToolSearch  query: "select:list_issues,save_issue,list_milestones,get_issue"
```

(Load only the ones the calling skill needs.)

## Operations

### `list-open`

```
list_issues  project: "<project>", query: "<keywords>", limit: 25
```

- Filter by `status` by passing the matching state group when the skill asks: `started` (In
  Progress), `unstarted` (Todo), `backlog`. orient pulls all three; drop-buoy searches across open
  work with `query`.
- Map each returned issue to the port shape:
  - `title` ← `title`
  - `handle` ← identifier (e.g. `JES-42`)
  - `url` ← `url`
  - `status` ← state type (`started` / `unstarted` / `backlog`)
  - `priority` ← `1=urgent, 2=high, 3=medium, 4=low, 0=none`
  - `mountain` ← the issue's milestone
  - `blocked` ← from relations; if a candidate's blocked status is load-bearing and unclear from the
    list, confirm with `get_issue … includeRelations: true` and read `blockedBy`.

### `recent-done`

```
list_issues  project: "<project>", state: "completed", limit: <n>, orderBy: "completedAt"
```

Map `title`, `handle` (identifier), `when` (`completedAt`), `mountain` (milestone).

### `capture`

```
save_issue  team: "<team>", project: "<project>", title: "...", description: "...",
            priority: <0-4 if known>
```

- `links` → `relatedTo` / `parentId` / `blocks` / `blockedBy`, each taking issue identifiers (e.g.
  `JES-4`), **not** titles. These relations are **append-only**.
- Before creating, search (`list-open` with the new task's keywords) and **update a near-duplicate
  instead** of creating a second issue. A duplicate is worse than a missing link.
- **Returns:** the new identifier (`handle`) and `url`.

### `update`

```
save_issue  id: "<handle>", state: "<new state>", ...   (pass id to update; omit to create)
```

- **Staleness gotcha:** `save_issue`'s response can echo the *pre-update* values — it's not
  confirming failure. To confirm a change landed, re-fetch with `get_issue`; don't retry blindly off
  the response.

### `log-decision`

Linear has no separate decision log. Record decisions as issue comments (`save_comment`) on the
relevant issue, or as a dedicated issue when there's no obvious anchor. (Most repos using Linear
won't invoke this operation.)

## Notes

- Assignee, if ever needed, is `"me"`.
- One project per effort. Creating new *projects* is `establish-tracking`'s job, not a capture.
- Capability Owners are **not** Linear issues. They're markdown in `owners/`, listed in
  `owners/INDEX.md` — the same in every repo. Only the adaptation tasks they spawn are captured
  here. (Owners used to be never-closed issues labeled `owner`; that's gone.)

input.title: "Choose your sleeves" — rectangular card frames and custom card backs on the Tabletop
input.description:
Let players pick sleeves for their deck as it appears on the Tabletop: a rectangular card frame (sleeve) around each card, and a custom sleeve image for card backs.

**Why it fits together:**
- A sleeve image is exactly what a face-down card needs — the back of a sleeved card *is* the sleeve.
- Sleeves / rectangular frames give cards square-legal corners, matching the site's square-corners style (physical cards stay rounded, but a sleeve edge is square).

**When to do it:** Lands naturally with the custom CardShape work at Tabletop Mountain 2 (see `apps/tabletop/SEAMAP.md`). Don't accelerate this — pick it up when CardShape happens; a sleeve is a natural first exercise of a custom shape's rendering.

**What surfaced it:** Buoy dropped during Tabletop v0 work (JES-127); listed under "Buoys to drop" in `notes/PLAN-tabletop-v0.md`.

**Related:** JES-79 covers choosing sleeve colors (inner & outer) on the Shuffler's deck preview page — same "personalize your play space" idea; this issue is the Tabletop-rendering half. Coordinate the two so the chosen sleeve shows up in both places.
